content_blueprint.copy_outline: Brief salutation acknowledging your expertise in managing adults with anti–AChR antibody–positive generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).
content_blueprint.section_summary: Simple greeting line tailored to neuromuscular specialists treating adults with generalized myasthenia gravis.
content_blueprint.clinical_fact_covered: None; this section is purely a professional salutation.

content_blueprint.headline: A long-acting complement option for appropriate adults with anti‑AChR+ gMG
content_blueprint.rationale: Frame the brand and clinical focus upfront.
content_blueprint.copy_outline:
- Introduce ULTOMIRIS (ravulizumab‑cwvz) as an option for your adult patients with anti‑AChR antibody–positive gMG.
- Signal that the email will focus on data for controlling the symptom journey based on a 26‑week trial.
content_blueprint.section_summary: Short text overview introducing ULTOMIRIS for adult patients with anti‑AChR antibody–positive gMG and the focus on symptom control.
content_blueprint.clinical_fact_covered: ULTOMIRIS is positioned for adult patients with anti‑AChR antibody–positive gMG, with symptom control assessed over 26 weeks.

content_blueprint.headline: More than 2x greater MG‑ADL improvement vs placebo at Week 26
content_blueprint.rationale: Deliver the core MG‑ADL efficacy story.
content_blueprint.copy_outline:
- In the randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled CHAMPION‑MG trial in adults with anti‑AChR+ gMG (ULTOMIRIS n=86; placebo n=89), ULTOMIRIS achieved a greater mean improvement in MG‑ADL total score at Week 26 than placebo (−3.1 vs −1.4; P<0.001), representing more than 2x greater improvement from baseline.
- MG‑ADL improvements with ULTOMIRIS were observed as early as Week 1 and were sustained over the 26‑week treatment period, with most patients remaining on background gMG therapies.
content_blueprint.section_summary: Concise text summary of CHAMPION‑MG design and primary MG‑ADL efficacy results, drawing on randomized trial text and figure claims.
content_blueprint.clinical_fact_covered: In CHAMPION‑MG, ULTOMIRIS produced statistically significant, more than 2x greater mean improvement in MG‑ADL vs placebo at Week 26, with onset by Week 1 and sustained effect through 26 weeks.

content_blueprint.headline: Clinician-assessed muscle strength: significant QMG improvements at 26 weeks
content_blueprint.rationale: Reinforce efficacy with clinician-assessed strength data.
content_blueprint.copy_outline:
- At Week 26, ULTOMIRIS showed a greater mean improvement in QMG total score vs placebo (−2.8 vs −0.8 points; 3.5‑fold greater improvement; P<0.001), reflecting improved global muscle strength.
- A higher proportion of ULTOMIRIS‑treated patients achieved a ≥5‑point QMG improvement at Week 26 vs placebo (30% vs 11.3%; P=0.005), with additional domain‑level QMG improvements reported as exploratory findings.
content_blueprint.section_summary: Brief text summary of QMG key secondary endpoint and responder analyses, based on trial text and associated figure claims.
content_blueprint.clinical_fact_covered: ULTOMIRIS demonstrated statistically significant improvements in QMG mean change and ≥5‑point responder rates vs placebo at Week 26, with exploratory support across ocular, bulbar, and limb domains.

content_blueprint.headline: Immediate, complete, and sustained terminal complement C5 inhibition through 26 weeks
content_blueprint.rationale: Link clinical effects to sustained C5 inhibition.
content_blueprint.copy_outline:
- ULTOMIRIS, the first and only long‑acting complement C5 inhibitor for anti‑AChR+ gMG, achieved complete inhibition of serum free C5 (below 0.5 µg/mL) by the end of the initial infusion and maintained it through 26 weeks in all treated adults.
- PK/PD data support weight‑based loading followed by maintenance dosing every 8 weeks, with a note that no direct efficacy or safety conclusions are drawn solely from these PK/PD analyses.
content_blueprint.section_summary: Short text summary of pharmacodynamic data showing ULTOMIRIS as a long‑acting C5 inhibitor achieving rapid and sustained free C5 suppression.
content_blueprint.clinical_fact_covered: ULTOMIRIS provides rapid and sustained terminal complement inhibition through 26 weeks in all studied adult patients, supporting an every‑8‑weeks regimen.

content_blueprint.headline: Safety profile and meningococcal risk considerations with ULTOMIRIS
content_blueprint.rationale: Balance efficacy with essential safety information.
content_blueprint.copy_outline:
- In adults with gMG receiving ULTOMIRIS across the randomized and open‑label periods, adverse reactions reported in ≥10% of patients included diarrhea and upper respiratory tract infection; serious adverse reactions occurred in 23% vs 16% with placebo, with infections the most common serious events, including a fatal case of COVID‑19 pneumonia and one infection leading to discontinuation.
- Because complement inhibition increases susceptibility to Neisseria meningitidis, ULTOMIRIS carries a risk of serious, potentially life‑threatening meningococcal infections and is available only through a REMS program requiring prescriber and patient enrollment.
content_blueprint.section_summary: Brief safety overview using tabular adverse reaction data and text describing common ARs, serious AEs, and REMS requirements for meningococcal risk.
content_blueprint.clinical_fact_covered: Key safety findings include common ARs ≥10%, serious AEs (notably infections), and the boxed meningococcal infection risk managed via a REMS program.
